seo_title: Calcutta HC: Financier's Loan Suit Is Commercial
title: Calcutta High Court Holds a Financier's Loan Recovery Suit Is Commercial Even Without a Mercantile Document
case_name: Sudha Kankaria v. Krishna Kumar Bhatter (HUF)
card_summary: A Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court set aside a decree ordering Sudha Kankaria to pay about Rs 83.97 lakh on an instalment loan from Krishna Kumar Bhatter (HUF). It held a financier's business lending is an 'ordinary transaction' under Section 2(1)(c)(i) of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015, needing no mercantile document, and returned the plaint to the Commercial Division.
card_tip: A lender pursuing recovery of a business loan in Kolkata should file before the Commercial Division under the Commercial Courts Act even if the loan was never recorded in a promissory note or other mercantile document.
verification_notes: The Division Bench of Justices Debangsu Basak and Aryak Dutt, the instalment loan history (2008-2009), the Rs 83.97 lakh decree under appeal, the return of the plaint to the Commercial Division, and the holding on 'ordinary transactions' under Section 2(1)(c)(i) of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 are reported consistently by LiveLaw Biz and Verdictum, with Court Kutchehry's case record agreeing on the parties and appeal number. Sources differ on the exact decision date: Court Kutchehry's record and the LiveLaw PDF filename both point to 13 November 2026, which the card uses; LiveLaw's own citation (2026 LLBiz HC (CAL) 267) was not independently cross-checked against a primary court record in this run.
